incumbent.name: Tonya Pfaff
incumbent.summary: Tonya Pfaff, a retired Terre Haute high school math teacher, has represented House District 43 since she was first elected in 2018 {caucus_pfaff}. She serves on the Ways and Means and Education committees and is ranking minority member of the Agriculture and Rural Development Committee {caucus_pfaff} {caucus_pfaff_cmte}.
record: Committees: Ways and Means; Education; Agriculture and Rural Development (ranking minority member) {caucus_pfaff_cmte}.

April 10, 2025: Voted no when the House passed SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law, 65-29 {rc_sea1_433}; she said it "offers very little to individual homeowners while shifting the burden to increased local income taxes" and that Vigo County "stands to lose $20.5 million" {caucus_pfaff_sb1}.

April 2025: Added an amendment requiring consent instruction in human sexuality curriculum to SB 442; after the language was removed in conference committee, it was restored in the final version passed April 23, 2025 {caucus_pfaff_sb442}.
April 25, 2025: Voted no on the 2025 state budget conference report (HEA 1001), adopted 66-27 {rc_hb1001_576}.
Dec. 5, 2025: Voted no when HB 1032, the mid-decade congressional redistricting bill, passed the House 57-41 {rc_hb1032_28}.

2026 session: Authored HB 1325, directing the education, child services, health and family and social services agencies to share data on services for children with special needs; it passed the House 93-0 and the Senate 45-0 and was signed Feb. 24, 2026 {caucus_pfaff_hb1325} {policyrisk_hb1325}. Jan. 28, 2026: Voted yes on HB 1002 (electric utility affordability), which passed 89-4 {rc_hb1002_149}.

race_context: House District 43 is in Vigo County {caucus_pfaff}; Pfaff's campaign describes it as covering Terre Haute, West Terre Haute and Seelyville {pfaff_site}.
Wikipedia's 2026 election summary notes Pfaff was re-elected without opposition in 2024 and that Donald Trump narrowly carried the district in 2024 {wiki_2026}.
Pfaff and Lore were the only candidates listed in their parties' May 5, 2026 primaries {wiki_2026}; both are on the November ballot {in_list}.

Key differences: Pfaff opposed the 2025 property-tax law, the 2025 budget and the 2025 redistricting bill and opposes universal private school vouchers {rc_sea1_433} {rc_hb1001_576} {rc_hb1032_28} {caucus_pfaff_vouchers}; Lore, a Vigo County school board member, emphasizes reducing administrative paperwork for schools, spending accountability and private-sector job growth {lore_issues}.
No general-election debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Amy Lore is a Vigo County School Board member and former board president with a background in communications and public policy {ts_lore} {lore_about}. She is running on school quality, spending accountability and economic growth {lore_issues}.
background: Elected to the Vigo County School Corporation board in 2020 and re-elected in 2024; board president 2023–2024 {lore_about}.
More than two decades in communications and public policy, including as an adviser and speechwriter to former Lt. Gov. Becky Skillman {ts_lore}.
Indiana State University graduate (bachelor's and master's in public administration); lives in Terre Haute's Farrington's Grove neighborhood {ts_lore} {lore_about}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as a Republican in early February 2026 {ts_lore}; the only Republican listed in the May 5, 2026 primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Wants to improve student results and teaching quality while reducing administrative paperwork and keeping decisions local; says "Every child needs access to high-quality education and the opportunity to succeed" {lore_issues}.
Supports cost-conscious government with fewer unnecessary rules; says "Hoosiers need practical solutions and responsible spending from their leaders" {lore_issues}.
Says "Government does not create jobs. It creates an environment where Hoosiers can create jobs" {lore_issues}.
Wants the state to support local partnerships among residents, institutions and businesses in Vigo County {lore_issues}.

on_incumbent: No statements by Lore about Pfaff or her record were found; her announcement said she is running to keep state government "focused on serving taxpayers" {ts_lore}.
plans: Said she is running to strengthen schools and grow economic opportunity {ts_lore}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements are listed on her website {lore_site}. No fundraising figures were found.
gaps: No specific positions found on property taxes, vouchers, redistricting, energy or data centers.
No news coverage after her February 2026 announcement was found.
Unverified: a Tribune-Star preview of March 2026 primary forums at the Vigo County Public Library may have listed Pfaff and Lore; the fetched text was inconsistent.

candidates.summary: Tonya Pfaff is the Democratic incumbent, first elected in 2018 and seeking a fifth term {caucus_pfaff} {ts_lore}. Her 2026 special-needs services bill became law, and she voted against the 2025 property-tax law, budget and redistricting bill {policyrisk_hb1325} {rc_sea1_433} {rc_hb1001_576} {rc_hb1032_28}.
background: Taught high school math for 32 years at Terre Haute South, West and North high schools, retiring in 2025 {caucus_pfaff}.
Bachelor's degree from Saint Mary-of-the-Woods College and master's from the University of Oklahoma; lives in Terre Haute {pfaff_about}.
path_to_ballot: The only Democrat listed in the May 5, 2026 primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Says "education funding for our schools, Indiana State University and Ivy Tech are the first priority" and that the teacher shortage "must be addressed" {pfaff_platform}.

Opposes universal private school vouchers, saying they "take funding meant for the kids in our public schools"; she cites a figure that Vigo County schools have lost more than $36 million since the program expanded {caucus_pfaff_vouchers}.

Opposed SEA 1 (2025), saying homeowners' savings would be offset by higher local income taxes and asking, "Of course everyone wants to pay less in property taxes, but at what cost?" {caucus_pfaff_sb1}.
Said the 2025 congressional maps "were not drawn to benefit Hoosiers, but to artificially boost the political performance of one party" {caucus_pfaff_redist}.
Says "Terre Haute and Vigo County must be aggressive in competing for jobs" and supports expanded vocational and apprenticeship programs {pfaff_platform}.
Says local roads depend on adequate state funding and calls for affordable high-speed broadband for every home and business {pfaff_platform}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Pfaff about Lore were found.
plans: Lists education and economic development for Terre Haute, West Terre Haute and Seelyville as her legislative goals {caucus_pfaff} {pfaff_site}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements are listed on her website {pfaff_site}. No fundraising figures were found.
gaps: No 2026 campaign news coverage or debate found.
No statements found on energy or data centers.
